{{short description|Croatian chemist}}
'''Franjo Kajfež''' ([[Martijanec]] near [[Ludbreg]], 15 February 1936 – [[Zagreb]], 23 April 2004) was a [[Croats|Croatian]] [[chemist]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hrvati koji su mijenjali svijet: Ima ih više nego slutite! - Politika+|url=http://www.politikaplus.com/novost/42018/hrvati-koji-su-mijenjali-svijet-ima-ih-vise-nego-slutite|accessdate=20 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Hrvati koji su promijenili svijet - Dnevnik.hr|url=http://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/tech/koliko-dobro-poznajemo-hrvate-koji-su-promijenili-svijet.html|accessdate=20 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=KAJFEŽ, Franjo - Hrvatski biografski leksikon - Leksikografski zavod Miroslav Krleža|url=https://hbl.lzmk.hr/clanak/9422|accessdate=20 July 2017}}</ref> Graduated (1959) and Ph.D. (1968) at the Faculty of Technology in [[Zagreb]]. Work at the [[Pliva|Pliva factory]] in Zagreb (1960) was director of the Institute of Medicines in [[Novi Sad]], [[Slovenia]] (1961–71) and director of the CRC Development Research Society in [[Switzerland]] (1971–1979). He was involved in the synthesis of organic compounds, especially chemical drugs. He was Minister of Industry, Naval Architecture and Energy (1992–1993), County of Krapina-Zagorje County (1993–1995) and Counselor of the President of the Republic for Local Self-Government and Technological Development (1995–2000). He was the owner of 88 patents and the author of 150 scientific papers.
